entries.answer: Judo is a Japanese grappling art in which a throw ends the exchange, and the aim is to put an opponent on their back rather than to hurt them, which is why holds to the neck are forbidden and why a match can be won without a single punch. Competitions are decided by a throw's completeness or by ground control measured in seconds, and the two scoring systems alternate between weight classes. A judo throw is only counted if the opponent lands on their back or side, so standing drop attacks are difficult.

patterns: how is a boxing match scored
entries.answer: Boxing is a combat sport in which the only thing that decides the outcome is where a punch lands, and the whole craft is making one land while none of yours do. Scoring is by counting clean blows to the head and body, judged by an official, and a knockdown does not stop the contest the way it does in some other sports. The gloves are small by design, being about 10 ounces, and the reason is historical: thin gloves force correct technique and make a punch land on the bone.

patterns: what is a stance in boxing
entries.answer: A stance is the standing position from which an exchange is fought, and it sets the range you can work at. In boxing there are orthodox and southpaw, differing by which foot leads, and the choice is made once and rarely changed. In kickboxing a squared stance allows both kicks and punches, while a long boxing stance does not. Getting a stance wrong costs more than any technique mistake, because every subsequent movement starts from it.

patterns: what does a black belt mean
how many belts are there in judo
do all martial arts use belts
entries.answer: In a belt-based martial art a belt is a visible rank, and the colour order is almost universal: white, then coloured, then black. In judo the coloured ranks run upward through a dozen or more levels, while in aikido or karate the number and the exact colours vary by organisation. The reason the system spread from judo is that black belt is a universally legible signal of a long training, which is useful in a room full of strangers.

patterns: what is a round in a fight
entries.answer: A round is one segment of a bout, separated by a rest period, and the number and length of rounds is a rule rather than a consequence of the contest. Championship boxing is twelve rounds of three minutes with one minute between, while a title fight may be scheduled for fewer, and the twelve-round format is the one that most shapes the sport's difficulty. The rest exists because the decision to continue is made with accumulated fatigue, and stamina is part of the contest.
